Are there any good reasons to support it?

Because the alternative isn't "no treaty", it's "Chinese-authored treaty", which is less advantageous (at least for Americans).

Is it all as bad as it sounds?

If you get your news from angry internet users, it sounds like it'll rape your wife and steal your firstborn. If that's the case, it's not all as bad as it sounds.

In fact, most of the (valid) complaints can be summed up in two reasons:

  1. The public does not have access to an official draft. As a result, people (a) don't know what is in the agreement, and (b) suspect foul play. It's important to note that we'll have access to the final draft for at least two months (and probably much longer) before Obama can sign it.

  2. There are some unpopular IP (intellectual property) provisions. If you're American, the vast majority of this will not affect you because it simply re-codifies existing aspects of US law; if you're not already violating US IP law, this won't change anything. That said, a lot of people have issues with the DMCA and other US laws, and this might make it harder to change those in the future.

As a side note, one complaint is that it will undermine national sovereignty, but to be blunt: that's fucking stupid. This is no different than any other treaty, except perhaps in scale.

Unless you're part of big business, you should be vehemently opposed to this. This "treaty" has only been constructed with the intent to grant even more power to our corporate overlords, and it needs to be stopped at all costs. It's infringing on the very foundation of America, and will surely end up exploiting the labor of the lower-class in many eastern countries as well.
